OpenStreetMap layers for New York City

Source: R/functions.R
nyc_osm.Rd

Each function returns a duckplyr-backed lazy data frame connected to a GeoParquet file bundled with this package, holding one layer of OpenStreetMap (OSM) features within 500 feet of New York City, from the Geofabrik extract of 18 October 2026.

Usage

nyc_osm_points(borough = NULL)

nyc_osm_lines(borough = NULL)

nyc_osm_buildings(borough = NULL)

nyc_osm_areas(borough = NULL)

nyc_osm_routes(borough = NULL)

Source

© OpenStreetMap contributors, https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright. Geofabrik extract new-york-261018, https://download.geofabrik.de/north-america/us/new-york.html.

Arguments

borough

NULL (the default) for all features, including those outside the boroughs, or one or more of "Manhattan", "Bronx", "Brooklyn", "Queens", and "Staten Island".

Value

A duckplyr data frame backed by GeoParquet.

Details

  • nyc_osm_points(): tagged nodes: points of interest (amenities, shops, restaurants), transit stops, crossings, street furniture, trees, and so on. 701,481 rows, 35 columns.

  • nyc_osm_lines(): open ways: streets, footways, cycleways, rail, waterways, barriers. 471,643 rows, 26 columns.

  • nyc_osm_buildings(): closed ways and multipolygon relations with a building tag. 1,089,132 rows, 22 columns.

  • nyc_osm_areas(): all other closed ways and multipolygon relations: land use, parks, leisure, water, natural features, and amenity areas such as parking lots and school grounds. 202,990 rows, 27 columns.

  • nyc_osm_routes(): route relations: bicycle, bus, train, subway, road, hiking, ferry, and other routes. 2,426 rows, 13 columns.

Use dplyr verbs to filter, select, and summarise, then call dplyr::collect() to bring results into R memory, and nyc_osm_to_sf() to convert them to an sf object. To pull other OSM tags out of tags into columns, use nyc_osm_add_tags().

Columns. Every layer has these columns:

osm_type

OSM element type: "node", "way", or "relation" (character).

osm_id

OSM element ID (double). IDs are unique only within an element type, so the key is osm_type and osm_id together. The element is at https://www.openstreetmap.org/<osm_type>/<osm_id>.

name, ...

A selection of common OSM tags, one column per tag, listed below (character). Column names are tag keys with : replaced by _, e.g. addr:street is addr_street. Values are as entered in OSM: NA means the tag is absent. Numeric-looking tags such as height, lanes, or building:levels are text, because OSM values can include units or lists (e.g. "12 m", "2;3").

tags

All OSM tags of the element, as a DuckDB MAP of key to value. After collecting, a list column of data frames with columns key and value.

borough

Borough of the feature: "Manhattan", "Bronx", "Brooklyn", "Queens", or "Staten Island" (character). The borough containing a point on the feature's surface; for buildings and areas that cross a borough line, the borough holding the largest share of the polygon's area. Boroughs are those of nycmaps::nyc_boros_sf, which follow the legal boundaries, so a few features differ from their address: piers built out from the Brooklyn shore into the East River, for example, are in Manhattan. NA for features within the 500 ft buffer but in no borough, e.g. on Ellis Island or in New Jersey or Nassau County.

osm_extract

Date of the OSM extract, 2026-10-18 (Date).

geometry

Geometry in EPSG:2263 (NAD83 / New York Long Island, US feet), as WKB (raw vector, list column after collecting). Points for nyc_osm_points(); LineStrings for nyc_osm_lines(); MultiPolygons for buildings and areas; MultiLineStrings for routes.

Tag columns by layer:

  • points: name, amenity, shop, cuisine, highway, public_transport, railway, leisure, tourism, natural, barrier, man_made, office, craft, healthcare, emergency, historic, place, brand, operator, opening_hours, website, phone, wheelchair, addr_housenumber, addr_street, addr_postcode, ref, wikidata.

  • lines: name, highway, service, footway, cycleway, surface, lanes, maxspeed, oneway, bridge, tunnel, layer, railway, waterway, barrier, access, bicycle, foot, ref, wikidata.

  • buildings: name, building, building_levels, height (in metres, the OSM convention), nycdoitt_bin (NYC Building Identification Number, from the import of city building footprints; joins to bin in the nycbuildings package), addr_housenumber, addr_street, addr_postcode, amenity, shop, leisure, tourism, historic, man_made, office, wikidata.

  • areas: name, amenity, shop, leisure, landuse, natural, water, tourism, historic, sport, man_made, office, boundary, admin_level, aeroway, military, place, addr_housenumber, addr_street, addr_postcode, wikidata.

  • routes: name, route, ref, network, operator, colour, wikidata.

What tags mean is documented on the OSM wiki, e.g. https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:amenity.

Coverage. Features are those in the bounding box -74.26, 40.49, -73.69, 40.92 that are within 500 feet of a borough boundary in nycmaps::nyc_boros_sf, so shoreline, pier, and bridge features are kept. Points are nodes with at least one tag other than source, created_by, and similar. Polygons are closed ways with a tag that implies an area (e.g. building, landuse, leisure, amenity) and multipolygon relations; a polygon with any building tag is in the buildings layer.

Storage. Buildings are stored as one file per borough (plus one for features outside the boroughs); nyc_osm_buildings() reads them as a single table, and its borough argument reads only the files needed. Files are sorted along a Hilbert curve, so spatial filters on nearby features read little data.

OSM and official sources. OSM is edited by volunteers. For authoritative NYC building footprints, streets, and boundaries, see the nycbuildings, nyclion/nycstreets, and nycmaps packages. Most OSM buildings in NYC were imported from the city's footprints, with building types, levels, and names added since. OSM adds points of interest, footways and cycleways, transit stops and routes, land use, and natural features.

Licence. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0. See https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright. The bundled data are a database derived from OSM and are also under the ODbL.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(dplyr)

# Restaurants by cuisine in Manhattan
nyc_osm_points(borough = "Manhattan") |>
  filter(amenity == "restaurant", !is.na(cuisine)) |>
  count(cuisine) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  collect()

# Cycleways in Brooklyn as sf lines
nyc_osm_lines(borough = "Brooklyn") |>
  filter(highway == "cycleway") |>
  collect() |>
  nyc_osm_to_sf()

# Buildings in Staten Island by type
nyc_osm_buildings(borough = "Staten Island") |>
  count(building) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  collect()
} # }
